questions.prompt: Students may use AI tools to help prepare responses during the assessed ESP tasks.
questions.explanation: The specification states that students may not use AI or any other tool designed to prepare a response, and internet access is not permitted during the assessed tasks.

source.reference: Spec p.56 Employer Set Project assessment overview

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the ESP pre-release task?
options: To become familiar with the industry context of the brief before the assessed tasks
To write the code that will be submitted
To complete the Gantt chart early
To receive marks for independent research
questions.explanation: The pre-release task is not directly assessed. It lets you research the sector (e.g. how digital technology is used) so you can apply it later.

questions.prompt: In the legacy 2022 ESP, notes made during the pre-release period could be taken into the supervised assessment sessions.
questions.explanation: The 2022 pre-release instructions said notes could be made but not taken into the supervised sessions. Always check the instructions for your own series.

source.reference: Legacy DPDD ESP (Elanp Air, Nov 2022) – paraphrased; check your current brief

questions.prompt: Staff work 7 hours a day, 5 days a week. How many hours can ONE person work in 14 weeks?
questions.explanation: 7 × 5 = 35 hours per week; 35 × 14 = 490 hours.
questions.commonMistake: Forgetting to multiply by the number of days per week.

questions.prompt: A 100-hour task is split equally between two developers working in parallel for 7 hours a day. How many working days does it take?
questions.explanation: Each developer does 50 hours. 50 ÷ 7 = 7.14 days, so the task needs 8 working days (a part day still needs to be scheduled).
questions.commonMistake: Rounding 7.14 down to 7, which does not leave enough time.

questions.prompt: A developer paid £45 per hour is assigned 95 hours of work. What is their cost to the project?
Which method correctly calculates the total staff cost for a project plan?
options: Add up each person's assigned hours multiplied by their own hourly rate
Multiply the total project hours by every person's hourly rate
Multiply the highest hourly rate by the number of staff
Use the same average rate for everyone
questions.explanation: The examiner report noted many plans multiplied total project hours by each person's rate. Costs must follow the hours each person is actually assigned in the Gantt chart.
questions.commonMistake: Charging every person for every hour of the project.

source.reference: Lead Examiner Report, ESP Autumn 2022 (legacy DPDD qualification)

questions.prompt: A cloud server with support costs £1,250 per month. What is the cost for the first year?
Current annual revenue is £1,400,000. A new system is expected to increase revenue by 3% in year 1. What is the forecast year 1 revenue?
questions.commonMistake: Giving only the increase (£42,000) instead of the new total.

questions.prompt: Year 1 revenue is £1,442,000. Annual outgoing costs are £1,175,000 and the one-off project cost is £150,000. What is the year 1 profit?
questions.explanation: 1,442,000 − 1,175,000 − 150,000 = £117,000. The examiner report noted students often forgot current outgoings when forecasting impact.

source.reference: Lead Examiner Report, ESP Autumn 2022 (legacy DPDD qualification)

questions.prompt: Put these tasks for one module in dependency order.
questions.explanation: Unit testing needs the module; integration testing needs tested units; acceptance testing needs the integrated system.

questions.prompt: In a project plan, creating the test plan can be scheduled after testing has finished.
questions.explanation: The examiner report highlighted test plans scheduled after testing as a common error. The test plan must exist before testing starts.

source.reference: Lead Examiner Report, ESP Autumn 2022 (legacy DPDD qualification)

questions.prompt: Which task must be complete before software modules can be deployed?
options: The server is installed and configured
questions.explanation: Deployment depends on the server existing. Identifying predecessor tasks is part of a logical Gantt chart.

questions.prompt: Breaking development into short sprints, with testing inside each sprint, is characteristic of which approach?
questions.explanation: The examiner report recommended breaking tasks into shorter sprints rather than putting all testing at the end.

source.reference: Lead Examiner Report, ESP Autumn 2022 (legacy DPDD qualification)

questions.prompt: Why include contingency (slack) time in a project plan?
options: To absorb delays such as extra faults or less experienced staff taking longer
To make the project cost less
Because staff need holidays in every week
questions.explanation: Contingency protects the deadline when risks happen.

questions.prompt: Justify planning for a senior engineer to review work done by a newly hired technician at the start of a project.
markPoints: The new technician is unproven or has only worked alongside senior staff before
Review reduces the risk of errors that would cause rework or delays
Errors found early are cheaper and quicker to fix, protecting the deadline
The review also develops the technician's skills for later tasks
questions.explanation: A rationale must justify decisions, not describe the plan. The examiner report gave this kind of risk-based allocation as an example of good justification.
questions.commonMistake: Just saying 'I assigned people based on their job title'.

source.reference: Lead Examiner Report, ESP Autumn 2022 (legacy DPDD qualification)

questions.prompt: Match each type of ESP test data to its description.
pairs: Normal data inside the accepted range
Data exactly at the edge of the accepted range that should be accepted
Data of the correct type outside the accepted range
Data just outside the edge of the accepted range
Data of the wrong type, e.g. text where a number is expected
questions.explanation: The ESP asks for valid, valid extreme, invalid, invalid extreme and erroneous test data (spec p.50).
questions.commonMistake: Confusing invalid with erroneous – a common problem in the examiner report.

source.reference: Spec p.50 Documenting the testing process

questions.prompt: A plane must be grounded if its previous maintenance job was LESS than 30 days ago. Which pair of values best tests this boundary?
questions.explanation: 29 days should ground the plane; 30 should not. Testing both sides of the boundary checks the logic (< vs <=).
questions.commonMistake: Only testing values far from the boundary, which would not find a < / <= mistake.

questions.prompt: What happens when the user enters 1?
options: 'Out of range' is printed even though 1 is a valid choice
questions.explanation: choice becomes 0, and 0 < 1 is True, so valid input is rejected. After subtracting 1 the valid indexes are 0–2, so the check should be choice < 0 or choice > 2.
questions.commonMistake: Checking the range against the menu numbers (1–3) after already converting them to indexes (0–2).

questions.prompt: What does this program output?
questions.code:
from datetime import datetime

previous = datetime.strptime("01/03/2024", "%d/%m/%Y")
current = datetime.strptime("30/03/2024", "%d/%m/%Y")
print((current - previous).days)
questions.explanation: Subtracting two datetime objects gives a timedelta; .days is the whole number of days between them.

questions.prompt:
The next service should be one year after the job date. What is wrong with this line?

temp_year = int(job_month) + 1
options: It adds 1 to the month instead of the year
questions.explanation: This is a logic error: the code runs, but the next service year is calculated from the month.
questions.commonMistake: Only fixing errors the IDE highlights – logic errors like this still run.

source.reference: Legacy DPDD ESP (Elanp Air, Nov 2022) – paraphrased; check your current brief

questions.prompt: What does this program output?
questions.explanation: Nothing separates the two strings, so they run together. Adding a newline character (\n) fixes the formatting – a defect in the legacy Task 2 text file output.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a SYNTAX error rather than a logic error?
options: A missing colon at the end of a def line
Adding 1 to the month instead of the year
questions.explanation: Syntax errors stop the program running and are usually highlighted by the IDE. Logic errors run but give wrong results.

questions.prompt: Put the parts of an ESP test log entry in a logical order.
items: Identify the test to be carried out
Describe the purpose of the test
Identify the test data to be used
Compare actual and expected results and state further action
questions.explanation: Spec p.50 lists these parts of the annotated testing evidence.

source.reference: Spec p.50 Documenting the testing process

questions.prompt: Explain why fixing only the errors highlighted by the IDE is not enough in ESP Task 2.
markPoints: The IDE only finds syntax errors (and some runtime errors)
Logic errors still run but give incorrect results, e.g. wrong date calculations or wrong range checks
Tests with normal, extreme and erroneous data against the requirements are needed to find them
questions.explanation: The mark scheme treats only fixing IDE-highlighted errors as limited understanding.

questions.prompt: Erroneous test data and invalid test data mean the same thing.
questions.explanation: Invalid data is the right type but outside the rules (e.g. 13 characters). Erroneous data is the wrong type (e.g. 'abc' for a number).

questions.prompt: In a flowchart, which symbol should represent a call to a reusable 'Get departure airport' routine?
questions.explanation: A sub-process (rectangle with double vertical lines) shows a separately defined routine – good evidence of decomposition and reuse.

questions.prompt: Describe how you would decompose a program that lets a user choose a flight route and date range, then see passenger number trends.
markPoints: Get and validate the departure airport from a numbered menu
Reuse the same routine to get and validate the destination airport
Get and validate the start and end dates, converting them to a date format
Load the CSV into a data frame inside a function
Filter the data for the chosen route and date range
Calculate totals or averages and output a table and a graph with meaningful labels
questions.explanation: The mark scheme suggests showing decomposition through algorithms for key processes presented as callable functions.

questions.prompt: Why should pseudocode avoid language-specific syntax such as curly braces and semicolons?
options: The design should be understandable by any developer, whatever language they use
Curly braces are illegal in flowcharts
questions.explanation: The examiner report recommended avoiding conventions specific to particular languages in designs.

source.reference: Lead Examiner Report, ESP Autumn 2022 (legacy DPDD qualification)

questions.prompt: A design says the menu choice must be 1–6. Which step prevents a crash when the user types 'abc'?
options: Check the input is a whole number before converting and comparing it
Convert the input with int() straight away
questions.explanation: Validating type before converting avoids a ValueError; then a range check handles numbers outside 1–6.

questions.prompt: What does this line do?
questions.code:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv("flights.csv")
options: Loads the CSV file into a pandas data frame
Creates a new empty CSV file
Plots the data as a graph
questions.explanation: pd.read_csv reads a CSV file into a data frame for processing (Appendix 2, pandas).

questions.prompt: Which line selects only flights from DUB to LHR?
questions.explanation: pandas combines conditions with & (and) or | (or), with each condition in brackets. Python's and/or keywords raise an error on a whole column.
questions.commonMistake: Using the and keyword with data frame columns.

questions.prompt: In a data frame whose last columns are daily passenger counts, what does extract.iloc[:, -7:] select?
options: All rows and the last 7 columns (the last 7 days)
questions.explanation: iloc[rows, columns]. : means all rows; -7: means from the 7th-from-last column to the end.

questions.prompt: days_df has one row per flight and one column per day. Which expression gives the total passengers across ALL flights and days?
questions.explanation: The first sum() totals each column (one total per day); the second adds those totals into one number. count() counts values, not passengers.

questions.prompt: Which Matplotlib line displays the graph window?
questions.explanation: plt.plot() creates the plot; plt.show() displays it.

questions.prompt: Which line selects only PM flights?
questions.explanation: A Boolean condition on the Time column selects matching rows.

questions.prompt: In the legacy flight data, some rows have 'MAN ' (with a trailing space) in the From column. What does df[df['From'] == 'MAN'] do with those rows?
options: It misses them, so Manchester totals are too low
It deletes them from the file
questions.explanation: 'MAN ' and 'MAN' are different strings. Cleaning the data first, e.g. df['From'] = df['From'].str.strip(), fixes it – the 'clean' step of data wrangling.
questions.commonMistake: Assuming the data provided is always clean.

questions.prompt: According to the examiner report, which is the best evidence of secure coding in the Task 4a dashboard?
options: Using local variables passed between functions and handling errors without exposing data
Adding a login screen before the menu
Putting the whole data frame in a global variable
Printing full error tracebacks to the user
questions.explanation: The examiner report stressed that a login function is NOT what is expected; secure coding and data practices are.
questions.commonMistake: Spending assessment time on a login screen.

source.reference: Lead Examiner Report, ESP Autumn 2022 (legacy DPDD qualification)

questions.prompt: Why use pd.to_datetime("01/04/22", dayfirst=True) with UK-format dates?
options: So 01/04/22 is read as 1 April 2022, not 4 January 2022
To convert the date to text
questions.explanation: Without dayfirst=True, pandas may read the first number as the month.

questions.prompt: Write Python (pandas) code that finds the departure airport with the most passengers in total, from a CSV with columns From, To, Time, then one column per day.
markPoints: Reads the CSV into a data frame inside a function
Cleans the From column (e.g. str.strip())
Selects the date columns and sums each row (e.g. iloc[:, 3:].sum(axis=1))
Groups by From and sums totals (e.g. groupby('From'))
Finds the largest total (e.g. idxmax() or sort_values) and outputs a meaningful message
questions.explanation: Self-mark against the steps. Try it for real in Python with pandas installed – the examiner report asks for more practice with pandas and Matplotlib.

source.reference: Lead Examiner Report, ESP Autumn 2022 (legacy DPDD qualification)

questions.prompt: Which sentence is EVALUATIVE rather than descriptive?
options: The numbered route menu meets the 'easy to use' requirement because users do not type airport codes, reducing input errors; however, users cannot compare two routes on one graph.
I made a menu with six airports.
My program uses pandas and Matplotlib.
First I loaded the CSV, then I made a graph.
questions.explanation: Evaluation makes a judgement against a requirement, supports it with an example, and considers limitations. The examiner report found most 4b answers were descriptive.

source.reference: Lead Examiner Report, ESP Autumn 2022 (legacy DPDD qualification)

questions.prompt: Which suggested future development is most relevant and justified?
options: Add preset date ranges (e.g. last 7 days, a chosen month) so users do not have to type dates, improving ease of use
Rewrite the program in another language
questions.explanation: Improvements should be meaningful, relevant to the scenario and linked to the requirements. This example comes from the examiner report.

source.reference: Lead Examiner Report, ESP Autumn 2022 (legacy DPDD qualification)

questions.prompt: A reflective evaluation should only discuss features that did not work.
questions.explanation: Also evaluate what worked, how well it met each requirement, and how successful features could be refined.

source.reference: Lead Examiner Report, ESP Autumn 2022 (legacy DPDD qualification)

questions.prompt: A dashboard prints a table of passenger numbers for a chosen route but has no graph. Evaluate how well it meets the requirement to 'display information in a meaningful way'.
markPoints: Strength: the table gives exact passenger numbers for the chosen route
Limitation: trends over time are hard to see in a table of numbers
Limitation: no graphical output, although the requirement mentions textual, numerical AND graphical output
Uses a specific example from the solution to support the judgement
Justified improvement, e.g. add a labelled line graph of passengers over time
Overall judgement of how well the requirement is met
questions.explanation: Evaluate = judgement supported by evidence against the requirement, plus justified improvements.
